 India face tricky WTC final road after South Africa's Cape Town Test win: Here's how
 India's WTC 2025-27 final hopes have taken a hit following South Africa's series-clinching win over Australia, leaving Shubman Gill's men with little room for error in their remaining seven Tests.
 Advertisement Shubman Gill's India have a tricky road ahead if they are to qualify for WTC final. Courtesy: Reuters By: India Today Sports Desk New Delhi , Oct 31, 2026 20:23 IST Last Updated Oct 31, 2026 20:23 IST Published by sabyasachi chowdhury Oct 31, 2026 20:23 IST Written By Sabyasachi Chowdhury India's road to the World Test Championship (WTC) 2025-27 final has become considerably tougher following South Africa's series-clinching victory over Australia in Cape Town. While the result has shaken up the points table, it has also underlined the challenge facing Shubman Gill's men, who have very little room for error in their remaining seven Tests.
 India are currently fourth in the standings with 68 points and a points percentage (PCT) of 51.52 after 11 matches. They have two Tests remaining against New Zealand away from home, followed by a five-match home series against Australia. With only the top two teams qualifying for the final, India will need a near-perfect finish to their campaign.

 The upcoming two-Test series against New Zealand could prove particularly important. If India win both matches, their PCT will rise to 58.97, giving them a much-needed boost. However, losing both Tests would bring their PCT down to 43.59, leaving them with an enormous challenge in the remaining five matches.
 Even winning all five Tests against Australia after losing both matches to New Zealand would take India only to 59.26 per cent. That could leave them dependent on results elsewhere.
 On the other hand, winning all seven remaining Tests would take India's PCT to 70.37, putting them in a strong position to challenge for a place in the final. Even six victories would give them 64.81 per cent. However, two or more defeats would make their qualification hopes considerably tougher.
 INDIA'S REMAINING TESTS IN WTC 2023-25 CYCLE
 New Zealand tour (Away) – 2 Tests 
 1st Test: November 19–23, 2026 – Wellington
 2nd Test: November 27–December 1, 2026 – Christchurch
 Australia tour of India (Home) – 5 Tests 
 1st Test: January 21–25, 2027 – Nagpur
 2nd Test: January 29–February 2, 2027 – Chennai
 3rd Test: February 11–15, 2027 – Guwahati
 4th Test: February 19–23, 2027 – Ranchi
 5th Test: February 27–March 3, 2027 – Ahmedabad
 NEW ZEALAND TAKE TOP SPOT, PROTEAS MOVE TO SECOND
 The latest standings have undergone a significant reshuffle following South Africa's 176-run victory over Australia in the third Test in Cape Town. Temba Bavuma's men clinched the series 2-1, taking their PCT to 71.42 and moving into second place.
 Australia, meanwhile, slipped from the top to third after their PCT dropped from 75 to 69.23 following the defeat. New Zealand have consequently moved to the top of the standings with 72.22 per cent, having collected 52 points from six Tests.
 India also moved up to fourth after Bangladesh's defeat against the West Indies in Mirpur, which pushed them down to fifth.
 With South Africa, New Zealand and Australia all occupying the top three positions, India's qualification equation has become increasingly complicated. Gill and Co. will need to take care of their own results while hoping their rivals drop crucial points in the remainder of the cycle. WTC POINTS TABLE AFTER CAPE TOWN TEST
 New Zealand: Matches – 6 | Won – 4 | Lost – 1 | Drawn – 1 | Points – 52 | PCT – 72.22%
 South Africa: Matches – 7 | Won – 5 | Lost – 2 | Drawn – 0 | Points – 60 | PCT – 71.43%
 Australia: Matches – 13 | Won – 9 | Lost – 4 | Drawn – 0 | Points – 108 | PCT – 69.23%
 India: Matches – 11 | Won – 5 | Lost – 4 | Drawn – 2 | Points – 68 | PCT – 51.52%
 Bangladesh: Matches – 7 | Won – 3 | Lost – 3 | Drawn – 1 | Points – 40 | PCT – 47.62%
 England: Matches – 16 | Won – 7 | Lost – 8 | Drawn – 1 | Points – 74 | PCT – 38.54%
 Sri Lanka: Matches – 6 | Won – 1 | Lost – 2 | Drawn – 3 | Points – 24 | PCT – 33.33%
 West Indies: Matches – 13 | Won – 3 | Lost – 8 | Drawn – 2 | Points – 42 | PCT – 26.92%
 Pakistan: Matches – 9 | Won – 2 | Lost – 7 | Drawn – 0 | Points – 5 | PCT – 4.63%
